newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks down in nerves over US jobs data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks down in nerves over US jobs data.

text.p: European bourses fell on Friday in nervous trading ahead of the release of U.S. jobless figures which will shed light on inflation pressures and interest rate prospects in the world's largest economy.
The dollar was virtually unchanged from Thursday's European closing levels as forex traders weighed the chances of higher interest rates if the data, due at 1230 GMT, showed strong growth in jobs.
London and Frankfurt stocks drifted lower in slow, early trading after scaling new peaks only two days ago as the jitters took hold. Paris, too, shed some of its recent gains.
London's FTSE 100 index was down 0.3 percent, getting little direction from Wall Street, which ended on negative ground at 5,932.85 after gaining 65 points in the past four sessions.

"There's not going to be a huge amount of tolerance for very strong numbers because of how far we've gone up," said one dealer. "From where we stand at the moment, there's more of a risk of an adverse reaction."
The closely-watched statistics on U.S. non-farm payrolls for September will provide a fresh picture of the power-house American economy.
A big increase in jobs could suggest inflationary pressures which may prompt the Federal Reserve central bank to tighten credit, bad news for business.
"But the fact remains that there's a lot of cash out there, and even if the numbers come in as expected, (stocks) can squeeze higher," the trader added.
Economists surveyed by Reuters expect an increase of 166,000 non-agricultural jobs in September after an upturn of 250,000 in August.
In Frankfurt, stocks slipped in thin trading on the floor and in computerised transactions ahead of the American data, with many traders taking a long weekend after Thursday's Unity Day holiday.
"Most people closed their books for the week on Wednesday ahead of the holiday." said one trader.
"Traders aren't going to want to stick their neck out ahead of the unemployment figures," said another.
French shares sagged 0.3 percent in early trading and dealers said the market was drifting ahead of the U.S. unemployment data.
The upcoming American figures also dominated the foreign exchanges which were quiet, with the dollar barely moving, and dealers reported no enthusiasm to break out of the current levels.

"The market would prefer to buy dollars. That's the attitude at the moment, but we still need some good figures today to determine the follow-through," said Alan Collins, head of technical analysis at Merita Bank.

But there was some ambiguity in market views. Strong data will add weight to the argument for higher near-term U.S. rates, which usually helps the dollar, but the likely gloom in the U.S. bond and stock markets could have the opposite effect.
"The converse would be likely in case of a soft figure, which would undermine the interest rate support the dollar enjoys," said Klaus Baader, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell economist.
Dealers said pre-weekend profit-taking had pared the lira's recent gains, but speculation of the Italian unit's entry to the ERM would keep it underpinned, said dealers.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.50 yen and 1.5303 marks versus Thursday's late European levels of 111.47 and 1.5291.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was down 13.6 points at 3,986.4.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 6.90 points at 2,129.19.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index was dowm 0.09 points at 2676.09. The computerised IBIS index was down 8.37 at 2676.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $380.20 an ounce in the morning, versus Thursday's close of $379.35. Silver was unchanged at $4.91.
